description.sr:
Spread (`...`) smo već videli kod nizova. Kod objekata on raspakuje svojstva objekta u novi objekat: `{ ...a, ...b }` pravi nov objekat sa svojstvima iz `a`, pa iz `b`. Ako isti ključ postoji u oba, pobeđuje onaj koji dolazi kasnije. Na primer, `{ ...{ x: 1, y: 2 }, ...{ y: 5 } }` daje `{ x: 1, y: 5 }`.

Napiši funkciju `mergeSettings(defaults, user)` koja spaja podrazumevana podešavanja sa korisničkim.

`defaults` i `user` su objekti. Funkcija vraća **nov** objekat u kome korisnička podešavanja prepisuju podrazumevana.

Pravila:
- ključ koji postoji samo u `defaults` ostaje, a ključ koji postoji samo u `user` se dodaje
- vrednosti `false`, `0` i `''` iz `user` takođe prepisuju
- ni `defaults` ni `user` se ne menjaju
- rezultat je uvek nov objekat, čak i kad je `user` prazan

Primeri:
- `mergeSettings({ theme: 'light', size: 12 }, { size: 14 })` → `{ theme: 'light', size: 14 }`
- `mergeSettings({ theme: 'light' }, { lang: 'sr' })` → `{ theme: 'light', lang: 'sr' }`
- `mergeSettings({ sound: true, volume: 5 }, { sound: false, volume: 0 })` → `{ sound: false, volume: 0 }`, jer su `false` i `0` prave vrednosti
- `mergeSettings({ a: 1 }, {})` → `{ a: 1 }`, kao nov objekat, različit od `defaults`
description.en:
We have already seen spread (`...`) with arrays. With objects it unpacks the properties of an object into a new object: `{ ...a, ...b }` creates a new object with the properties from `a`, then from `b`. If the same key exists in both, the one that comes later wins. For example, `{ ...{ x: 1, y: 2 }, ...{ y: 5 } }` gives `{ x: 1, y: 5 }`.

Write a function `mergeSettings(defaults, user)` that merges the default settings with the user's settings.

`defaults` and `user` are objects. The function returns a **new** object in which the user's settings overwrite the defaults.

Rules:
- a key that exists only in `defaults` stays, and a key that exists only in `user` is added
- the values `false`, `0` and `''` from `user` overwrite too
- neither `defaults` nor `user` is changed
- the result is always a new object, even when `user` is empty

Examples:
- `mergeSettings({ theme: 'light', size: 12 }, { size: 14 })` → `{ theme: 'light', size: 14 }`
- `mergeSettings({ theme: 'light' }, { lang: 'sr' })` → `{ theme: 'light', lang: 'sr' }`
- `mergeSettings({ sound: true, volume: 5 }, { sound: false, volume: 0 })` → `{ sound: false, volume: 0 }`, because `false` and `0` are real values
- `mergeSettings({ a: 1 }, {})` → `{ a: 1 }`, as a new object, different from `defaults`

text.sr:
Ovde pravimo (deklarišemo) funkciju. Funkcija je imenovan komad koda koji možemo da pozovemo koliko god puta hoćemo, svaki put sa drugim ulazom.

- `function mergeSettings` pravi funkciju sa tim imenom. Test je poziva baš tim imenom, pa mora biti napisano tačno ovako (velika i mala slova se razlikuju).
- `(defaults, user)` je lista parametara. Parametar je prazno „mesto“ za ulaz: `defaults` je objekat sa podrazumevanim podešavanjima, `user` je objekat sa podešavanjima koja je korisnik promenio. Poziv `mergeSettings({ size: 12 }, { size: 14 })` daje `defaults = { size: 12 }` i `user = { size: 14 }`.
- `{` otvara telo funkcije, a zatvara ga `}` u liniji 3.

Sama deklaracija ništa ne računa. Kod iz tela se izvršava tek kad funkciju pozovemo.
text.en:
Here we create (declare) a function. A function is a named piece of code that we can call as many times as we like, each time with different input.

- `function mergeSettings` creates a function with that name. The test calls it by exactly this name, so it must be spelled exactly like this (letter case matters).
- `(defaults, user)` is the parameter list. A parameter is an empty “slot” for input: `defaults` is the object with the default settings, `user` is the object with the settings the user changed. The call `mergeSettings({ size: 12 }, { size: 14 })` gives `defaults = { size: 12 }` and `user = { size: 14 }`.
- `{` opens the function body, and `}` on line 3 closes it.

The declaration itself computes nothing. The code in the body runs only when we call the function.

text.sr:
Spajamo oba objekta u jedan nov.

- `{ ... }` pravi nov objekat, pa se nijedan ulaz ne menja.
- `...defaults` upisuje u njega sva svojstva iz `defaults`.
- `...user` posle toga upisuje svojstva iz `user`. Ako ključ već postoji, nova vrednost ga prepisuje. Zato redosled odlučuje ko pobeđuje: `user` je napisan drugi, pa pobeđuje.
- Vrednosti `false`, `0` i `''` se prepisuju kao i svaka druga, jer spread ništa ne filtrira.
- Prazan `user` ne dodaje ništa, ali rezultat je i dalje nov objekat.

```
defaults = { theme: 'light', size: 12 }, user = { size: 14 }
posle ...defaults: { theme: 'light', size: 12 }
posle ...user:     { theme: 'light', size: 14 }
```
text.en:
We merge both objects into one new object.

- `{ ... }` creates a new object, so neither input is changed.
- `...defaults` writes into it all the properties from `defaults`.
- `...user` then writes the properties from `user`. If a key already exists, the new value overwrites it. That is why the order decides who wins: `user` is written second, so it wins.
- The values `false`, `0` and `''` are overwritten like any other, because spread filters nothing.
- An empty `user` adds nothing, but the result is still a new object.

```
defaults = { theme: 'light', size: 12 }, user = { size: 14 }
after ...defaults: { theme: 'light', size: 12 }
after ...user:     { theme: 'light', size: 14 }
```

text.sr:
Zatvara telo funkcije otvoreno u liniji 1.

- `}` je par za `{`. Svaka otvorena `{` mora da ima svoju `}`; ako jedna fali, kod se ne može pročitati (`SyntaxError`).
text.en:
Closes the function body opened on line 1.

- `}` is the pair of `{`. Every opened `{` must have its `}`; if one is missing, the code cannot be read (`SyntaxError`).

note.sr: Spread je plitak: radi za ovakva podešavanja, ali ne spaja ugnježdene objekte.
note.en: Spread is shallow: it works for settings like these, but does not merge nested objects.

text.sr:
`Object.assign(cilj, izvor1, izvor2, ...)` kopira svojstva iz izvora u prvi objekat (cilj) i vraća taj cilj.

- Prvi argument je `{}`, prazan novi objekat. On je cilj, pa se kopiranjem menja samo on, a ne `defaults` ni `user`. Da smo napisali `Object.assign(defaults, user)`, izmenili bismo `defaults`, a to je greška.
- Prvo se kopiraju svojstva iz `defaults`, pa iz `user`; kasniji izvor prepisuje raniji, isto kao kod spread-a.
- Rezultat je isti kao `{ ...defaults, ...user }`.
text.en:
`Object.assign(target, source1, source2, ...)` copies the properties from the sources into the first object (the target) and returns that target.

- The first argument is `{}`, an empty new object. It is the target, so only it is changed by the copying, not `defaults` or `user`. If we had written `Object.assign(defaults, user)`, we would have changed `defaults`, and that is a mistake.
- First the properties from `defaults` are copied, then from `user`; a later source overwrites an earlier one, the same as with spread.
- The result is the same as `{ ...defaults, ...user }`.
